director.summary: Moriarty Group delivered mixed performance across three stores this week (28-Sep-2026), with total retail sales of €133.2M YTD but declining -2.1% vs LY. Skerries leads on growth (+3.65% TY, +2.08% YTD) and highest basket value (€25.98), while Balbriggan shows strongest sales momentum (+11.13% TY) despite transaction decline. Waste reduction is positive across all stores (-42.9% to -38.2% TY vs LY), but margin compression remains a headwind with YTD scan margin declining €184k across the group.

stores.name: Palmerstown
stores.summary: Solid performer with TY sales +2.04% (€44.4k) and margin improvement +0.76% to 19.49%, but YTD sales down -1.99% (€-281k). Waste management excellent: -42.95% YTD reduction vs LY. Transaction count flat (+0.72% TY) indicates stable foot traffic.

stores.name: Balbriggan
stores.summary: Strongest TY sales momentum at +11.13% (€3.7k) with average spend up 11.97% to €22.10, but YTD trend negative at -2.26% (€-276k). Waste management excellent at -38.18% YTD; transaction decline of -0.76% TY signals traffic softness requiring attention.

stores.name: Skerries
stores.summary: Best performing store: TY sales +3.65% (€1.8k), only store with positive YTD growth +2.08% (€+298k), and highest basket value €25.98 (+5.23% TY). Critical issue: waste spike +74.45% TY (€+141k), worst performer in group requiring immediate investigation.

cross.title: Basket Value vs Traffic Paradox
cross.why: Skerries achieving €25.98 avg spend (+5.23% TY) while losing -1.57% TY transactions (2,011 vs 2,043); Balbriggan opposite (high TY transactions +11.31% but declining YTD -3.01%). This suggests different customer profiles or promotional strategies causing mix distortion.
cross.action: Conduct customer demographic and category mix analysis by store: is Skerries losing value customers to competitors while retaining premium buyers? Balbriggan may be attracting price-sensitive traffic. Align promotional calendars to defend high-value customer base and optimize category bundles per store profile.

cross.title: Waste Reduction Success Masking Operational Risk
cross.why: All three stores report impressive waste cost reductions (-38% to -75% TY), but Skerries' 74% 'improvement' is actually +141.4k euro absolute waste increase. This indicates waste is being categorized inconsistently or reduced forecasting/ordering is creating stockouts compensated by excessive shrink elsewhere.
cross.action: Standardize waste definition and reporting across all stores; implement weekly waste category breakdown (spoilage vs markdown vs damage) with photos; audit if waste reduction is from better forecasting or just reclassification; reconcile to inventory shrink variance.

cross.title: Margin Compression Despite Sales Growth
cross.why: Balbriggan +11.13% TY sales (+€3.7k) yet margin declined -€72.5k YTD; Skerries +3.65% TY (+€1.8k) yet margin down -€37k YTD. This indicates promotional discounting or SKU mix shift toward lower-margin categories is eroding profitability. Sales growth is hollow without margin discipline.
cross.action: Mandate category-level profitability reporting: identify which departments drove Balbriggan's 11.97% basket uplift; if high-volume/low-margin (e.g., loss leaders), re-calibrate promotion strategy. For Skerries, audit if +3.65% growth came from premium categories (margins +) or value lines (margins -). Implement promotional ROI tracking to ensure discounts drive profitable sales, not just volume.

diagnosis.wrong: Skerries waste spike is the critical operational failure: +74.45% TY (€141.4k) and +€15.2k YTD deterioration indicates systematic control breakdown in fresh/perishable departments. Simultaneously, group margin compression of €184k YTD across all stores, combined with transaction declines (Balbriggan -20.2k YTD, Skerries -1.57% TY), signals that store-level operational discipline and traffic generation are failing despite positive headline sales momentum in some cases.
diagnosis.why: Root causes: (1) Skerries likely experiencing either over-ordering (leading to spoilage), poor FIFO discipline (shelf-life rotation failures), or receiving damage not caught at intake; (2) Margin compression suggests promotional discounting is excessive relative to cost recovery—Balbriggan's 11.97% basket uplift may be driven by margin-destructive bundles rather than premium mix; (3) Transaction declines indicate foot traffic is being lost to competitors, suggesting pricing positioning or promotional timing is misaligned; (4) Waste reduction 'success' is statistical artifact—absolute waste pounds/value is not declining, just categories are being reclassified.
diagnosis.fix: Immediate: (1) Deploy Skerries operations audit today—audit all produce/dairy received, dated, and disposed in past 7 days with photographic evidence; implement 2x daily waste counts with department accountability; (2) Conduct margin analysis by promotional period and category at Balbriggan—quantify discount depth vs. cost of sales and identify margin-destructive promotions; (3) Standardize waste categorization across all stores and reconcile to inventory shrink variance to ensure real vs. reporting gains; (4) Launch footfall recovery program at Balbriggan with geo-targeted marketing and loyalty incentives to reverse -20k transaction YTD trend.
